claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me the names and ages of the children you're inquiring about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 9 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'm happy to help you assess eligibility for your son Alex.

To determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to gather some information about your circumstances. Let me start with the first question:

**Are you currently residing in the United Kingdom?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

**Are you responsible for Alex's care and do you have him living with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me and I'm responsible for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

**Is Alex in full-time education or approved training, or does he have any serious illness or disability?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's only 9, so he's just in primary school doing normal school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

**Are there any circumstances where Alex is not living with you full-time, such as being in care, living with another parent, or spending significant time elsewhere?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he lives with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that confirmation.

**Have you claimed Child Benefit for Alex before, and if so, is there any reason your claim might have been stopped or suspended?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I haven't claimed it before - that's why I'm asking now to see if I'm eligible.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

**What is your current annual income (or household income if you have a partner)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Why do you need to know my income? I thought I was just checking if I'm eligible for Child Benefit?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a very fair question! You're right to ask. 

While the basic eligibility criteria for Child Benefit don't depend on income, there is an additional consideration called the "High Income Child Benefit Charge" that applies if your income (or your partner's income if you have one) exceeds a certain threshold. This doesn't make you ineligible for Child Benefit itself, but it does affect how much you receive.

However, I realize I should clarify: are you asking whether you qualify for Child Benefit at all, or are you also interested in understanding what you might actually receive? If you're primarily interested in whether you're eligible to claim it in principle, I may have already gathered enough information to give you an answer.

Which would be more helpful for you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I just want to know if I'm eligible to claim it. I can worry about the amounts and taxes later if I need to.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, that makes sense! In that case, I have enough information to give you your eligibility assessment for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- You live in the UK
- You're a British citizen
- Alex lives with you full-time and you're responsible for his care
- He's 9 years old and in primary school
- You haven't had a previous claim stopped or suspended

You meet all the core eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news!** You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. 

You meet all the core eligibility requirements, and there are no barriers to your claim. You can go ahead and apply for Child Benefit for your son. When you're ready to claim, you'll need to contact HMRC or apply online through their system.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
